title: Privileged Access Review + Billing Reconciliation Sync
customer_attendees: Samir Patel - Head of Cloud Infra
topics: privileged access review for service accounts and SSH keys
billing reconciliation discrepancies for May cloud spend
KMS key rotation plan and access controls
audit log retention and SOC2 alignment
summary: Cross-functional sync to reconcile an unexpected May billing variance, run a quick privileged access audit for long-lived service accounts, agree on KMS rotation windows, and assign remediation tasks. Key ask: margin of error in billing + ensure no service accounts with blanket project roles remain. Action owners and deadlines captured.
action_items: Jonah -> scan GitHub for long-lived service account keys, open ticket with examples -> due 2026-06-19
Priya -> produce line-item billing export for May with cost centers and tag mapping -> due 2026-06-18
Maya -> validate autoscaler and burst pool metrics against the billing spike and share CSV -> due 2026-06-20
Alex -> schedule KMS key rotation maintenance window and notify stakeholders -> due 2026-06-22
Samir -> confirm VPC egress cost attribution and provide network flow logs link -> due 2026-06-21
next_steps: Share billing CSV and tagging doc in #finance-ops by EOD 6/18
Jonah to post GitHub findings and proposed least-privilege changes in the infra board ticket
Set follow-up 30-min check-in week of 6/22 to validate remediation
Legal to review any potential customer-impacting exposures and advise communications
transcript:
[00:00] Alex: alright, um, good afternoon everyone, thanks for jumping on. we'll try and keep this tight, it's 75 minutes on the calendar but i expect, uh, maybe 60. agenda is billing variance in May and a quick privileged access sweep; want to make sure the action items are clear at the end.
[00:18] Priya: sounds good, i'll start with the billing bits — we noticed a ~18% uptick in cloud spend for May versus our weekly run rate baseline, and it's not explained by the scheduled model rollouts. i have a preliminary breakdown but need to tie it to cost centers.
[00:34] Jonah: okay, did you already check autoscaling spikes? sometimes the burst pool misconfiguration causes double-billing when instances spin up long and then get replaced.
[00:41] Maya: yeah we saw a series of ephemeral pods in the redwood-inference-burst namespace — they were retried a few times, but it didn't look enough to justify 18%. also, there's a weird pattern around 05/12 where sequence length distribution spiked — could be eval sweeps.
[00:55] Priya: i pulled the high-level, but the tags are messy. we have dev/stage/prod but some teams use project tags and others don't, so need to map who owns which line item.
[01:10] Alex: okay, combine the tag map with the autoscaler logs. Maya, can you grab the burst metric CSV and drop in the shared drive? link in the notes.
[01:18] Maya: yeah i'll drop it, um, within the hour.
[01:22] Samir: quick thing on network egress — last month we had a VPC peer replication job that got rescheduled a few times, there were big NAT egress bytes, might be part of it. i can pull VPC flow logs.
[01:31] Priya: perfect, that might explain cross-region charges.
[01:34] Jonah: shifting to privileged access: we ran a quick look at service accounts and some long-lived keys — there are a handful of terraform state service accounts with owner-level roles. that's a no-go.
[01:46] Lena: owner-level for infra automation? that seems risky, are there known compensating controls?
[01:50] Jonah: not really; we have some IAM policies and constraints but those SA's had broad permissions. one of them dates back to 2023 and wasn't rotated.
[02:00] Alex: okay we need a prioritized list: which service accounts are in production, which have owner roles, and which are used by scheduled jobs. Jonah, can you run a script to enumerate and classify?
[02:09] Jonah: yes, i'll run the scan against IAM and GitHub and match keys. warning — the scan will produce false positives because some ephemeral CI keys look similar, but i'll vet them.
[02:18] Priya: can you also include cloud build/service account usage patterns? some of the billing is tied to CI runs.
[02:24] Jonah: yep.
[02:26] Chris: on the billing side, two small anomalies — a 03:00 AM job that ran for 7 hours on 5/12 and a data egress job that had an unexpectedly large output; both are in separate tickets but might link to the same pipeline.
[02:40] Maya: that 7-hour job is the k8s indexer; there was a retry storm after a node upgrade, and logs show repeated container restarts every ~30s. i filed infra-1234 but maybe we need to escalate.
[02:52] Alex: escalate if there was customer impact, but even without customer impact we need root cause and a permanent mitigation — maybe change restart policy or fix node drain hooks.
[03:03] Jonah: for KMS rotation, what's the SLAs? we currently rotate monthly for dev keys, quarterly for production. are we comfortable moving prod to monthly?
[03:13] Lena: legal prefers quarterly but if security says monthly reduces risk we can justify as a security control, just need to track downtime windows.
[03:21] Samir: rotating KMS keys for model artifacts has a coupling risk — we need to ensure old keys maintain decrypt capability for KV caches during overlap. otherwise we could break cached checkpoints.
[03:33] Maya: good point, the KV cache uses server-side encryption with customer-managed keys; i can validate the fallback logic. if rotation doesn't preserve the previous key in the key-ring, the cache won't decrypt.
[03:45] Jonah: so rotation procedure: schedule, snapshot key policies, make sure service accounts have get/decrypt on both keys during overlap window, rotate, verify, then deprecate old key. i'll draft runbook steps.
[03:57] Priya: back to billing — i need the full GCP/AWS line item export filtered to our accounts. can someone share the billing export path?
[04:05] Maya: it's in the finance-buckets/billing/2026/05/raw.csv — i'll grant read to finance-ops.
[04:11] Priya: perfect.
[04:13] Alex: action: Priya will produce the tagged mapping, Maya will confirm autoscaler and cache behaviors, Jonah will scan for long-lived keys and outline KMS rotation runbook. Samir to pull flow logs for VPC egress.
[04:26] Samir: on flow logs, there's a large transfer to a partner S3 endpoint on 5/12; i need to confirm if that was expected replication or an accidental sync.
[04:36] Chris: that sync was triggered by a manually invoked snapshot, i think. need to talk to platform services.
[04:40] Jonah: small request — can we enforce blocking policy for owner role on service accounts unless there's a documented exception? github audit should prevent owner bindings in terraform but we have legacy accounts.
[04:52] Lena: legal asks that exceptions be time-bound and approved; also want an audit trail.
[04:58] Alex: agreed. we'll treat the exception process like: short-lived token, ticket with approver, auto-expire.
[05:05] Priya: any customers impacted? i don't think so but we should do a sweep to confirm no exported customer data was involved in the egress job.
[05:12] Maya: i'll check S3 object logs and object-level ACLs; if anything looks off i'll flag it immediately.
[05:17] Jonah: middleware note — our logging retention for audit events is 90 days. for SOC2 we want 1 year; do we have the budget?
[05:24] Priya: finance may need to allocate more for storage; i'll model the incremental cost if we bump to 1 year.
[05:30] Alex: prioritize critical audit trails for 1-year retention and keep others at 90 for now.
[05:35] Samir: i want to call out service account used by legacy metrics exporter — it has compute admin. i'll open a ticket to restrict scope to metric-reading only.
[05:44] Jonah: also, in GitHub actions we found secrets imported via encrypted env, but there were 3 plaintext tokens in an old branch — i've already rotated them but we should ensure branch protection and secret scanning is enabled org-wide.
[05:57] Maya: is the scanning policy enabled? we enabled secret scanning a while back but not for forks or all repos.
[06:03] Jonah: partial coverage; i'll put a remediation plan for full org coverage.
[06:09] Priya: time check — 30 minutes left. can we list owner-specific tasks and due dates?
[06:14] Alex: yes. Jonah, find keys and propose least-privilege changes by Friday. Priya, billing mapping by Thursday. Maya, autoscaler + KV encryption verification by Monday. Samir, flow logs by Sunday. Lena, legal to confirm exception process by next Wednesday.
[06:28] Chris: small clarification: for the backup job egress to partner S3, who approved that?
[06:34] Samir: i'll look into approval chain; it may have been approved by a now-rotated IAM user, odd.
[06:39] Lena: if approvals are stale we should record that as an internal control gap for the next SOC2 readout.
[06:45] Jonah: also want to add MFA enforcement for any user granting owner roles; that should be in the short-term plan.
[06:51] Alex: yes, enforce MFA, ticketing for exceptions only.
[06:54] Priya: can we also get a reconciliation of committed reserved instances vs on-demand overspend? some of the spike could be due to misapplied commitments.
[07:03] Maya: i'll pull reserved capacity utilization for the last 90 days and share.
[07:08] Alex: excellent. two quick notes — one: Jonah, when you post your findings include the diff of IAM bindings and link to the relevant terraform module; two: Priya, when you post the billing CSV, include a column for suspected root cause and confidence level.
[07:20] Jonah: will do.
[07:23] Lena: legal question — if there is any customer data egress, do we have an obligation to notify customers? depends on contracts, but likely yes for PII. i'll review contract clauses.
[07:34] Priya: i'll flag any row with data egress and mark for legal review.
[07:37] Alex: wrap-up: recap of action items and follow-up meeting — same group, 30 minutes next week to validate remediations. thanks everyone.
[07:46] Maya: thanks, bye.
[07:47] Jonah: thanks.
[07:48] Samir: bye.
[07:49] Priya: bye.

Note: transcription includes some misheard words (e.g., K-M-S sometimes transcribed as "KMS"/"K M S", repo names abbreviated). Links referenced: finance-buckets/billing/2026/05/raw.csv, infra-1234 ticket (internal), infra board ticket (to be created).
